basis: Axonal neuropathy with a copper metabolism defect; ptosis and exotropia occur in 30-79%; muscle weakness and atrophy are neurogenic.
Defined by congenital structural heart disease caused by RBFOX2 variants.
Tumor originates in testicular germ cells; reproductive organs have no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy with neuromyotonia; muscle symptoms reflect nerve dysfunction; fixed contractures and muscle atrophy are reported in fewer than 30%.
Vibration-triggered mast-cell-mediated cutaneous and subcutaneous angioedema; laryngeal involvement is not established in at least 30%.
Benign epithelial tumor confined to the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Predisposition to breast and ovarian cancers, both outside the axes; cancer risks do not establish existing organ damage.
Intellectual developmental disorder with brain abnormalities; kyphoscoliosis affects 4/8 patients (50%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.
Oocyte maturation failure causes infertility; reproductive dysfunction without demonstrated endocrine disease has no axis.
Early-onset lens opacity defines this nonsyndromic cataract group.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines the group; additional organ damage varies across syndromes and is not established across most patients.
Definition specifies nonsyndromic sensorineural deafness; vestibular dysfunction shares the otologic axis. Historical Usher synonyms do not establish retinal disease.
Open spinal neural tissue and Chiari II malformation define neurologic disease; the accompanying spina bifida is a vertebral closure defect.
Deafness, cataracts and skeletal/muscle abnormalities define the syndrome; arrhythmia occurs in 80-99%. Delayed sexual maturation alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Intellectual disability with hypotonia; myopia in 50% and strabismus in 33%; congenital heart defects collectively affect about half. Hearing loss at 25% is excluded.
Ewing-family tumor arising in soft connective tissues; neural differentiation does not establish peripheral nerve origin.
Choroidal atrophy with visual impairment and ectodermal abnormalities of hair and nails defines the syndrome; middle-ear disease is occasional.
Bone fragility, recurrent fractures and skeletal deformities define CRTAP-related osteogenesis imperfecta; blue sclerae alone do not establish ocular functional damage.
Pregnancy implanted in the fallopian tube is an obstetric and reproductive condition; hemorrhage is a complication, not a defining blood disorder.
Exercise-triggered systemic hypersensitivity; transient cutaneous, respiratory and circulatory manifestations do not establish lasting damage to additional organs.
Neoplasm originates in the anus or anal canal; lymphoma and melanoma are individual subtypes, not mechanisms shared across this umbrella.
Malignant B-cell lymphoid neoplasm, primarily nodal; lymphoma requires the immune axis. Additional organ infiltration is not common enough across the group.
Tumor family predominantly arising in bone or soft connective tissues; neural differentiation and rare CNS subtypes do not establish common neurologic involvement.
Axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy; weakness is neurogenic. Scoliosis and fixed foot deformities occur in fewer than 30%.
Congenital absence of nails and microcephaly define the syndrome despite normal intelligence; widely spaced teeth alone do not establish GI damage.
